works.title: Enter Freely and of Your Own Free Will
works.source: Bram Stoker, Dracula (1897) · Project Gutenberg #345 · public domain
works.note: Jonathan Harker arrives at the castle: the heavy door, the courtly welcome, the hand cold as ice — and, from the valley, the howl of wolves. “Listen to them — the children of the night. What music they make!”

works.title: The Thing on the Wall
works.source: Bram Stoker, Dracula (1897) · Project Gutenberg #345 · public domain
works.note: Harker, a prisoner, looks out and sees his host emerge from a window and descend the sheer castle wall face-down, cloak spread like wings — “just as a lizard moves along a wall.”

works.title: The Three Sisters
works.source: Bram Stoker, Dracula (1897) · Project Gutenberg #345 · public domain
works.note: The vampire brides close upon the sleeping Harker, until the Count bursts in with terrible fury: “How dare you touch him… This man belongs to me!”

works.title: The Bloofer Lady
works.source: Bram Stoker, Dracula (1897) · Project Gutenberg #345 · public domain
works.note: A Westminster Gazette clipping: small children of Hampstead Heath stray after dark, lured by a “bloofer lady,” and return with a tiny wound at the throat.

works.title: Van Helsing on the Un-Dead
works.source: Bram Stoker, Dracula (1897) · Project Gutenberg #345 · public domain
works.note: The professor’s catalogue of the vampire’s powers and limits — the strength of many, no shadow, no mirror-image, the shapes of wolf and bat and mist — yet bound by laws he cannot break.

works.title: The Death of the Count
works.source: Bram Stoker, Dracula (1897) · Project Gutenberg #345 · public domain
works.note: The chase ends at sunset below the castle: the Kukri and the bowie knife, the body crumbling to dust — and, in that last instant, a look of peace upon the face.

works.title: Dracula’s Guest — complete
works.source: Bram Stoker, Dracula’s Guest and Other Weird Stories (1914) · Project Gutenberg #10150 · public domain
works.note: A traveller defies his coachman’s dread of Walpurgis Night and is overtaken by storm and wolf — saved by a message from a distant Boyar. Long taken for the deleted first chapter of the novel.

works.title: Dracula’s Guest and Other Weird Stories
